tags.name: web-session
tags.description: Use the HTTPS origin of the installed Web app as WEB_ORIGIN. The installation selects OIDC or Kubernetes bearer-token browser sessions. OIDC redirects the browser through its configured identity provider. A token session exchanges a Kubernetes bearer token for a cookie in one Web API replica. Choose the mode configured for the installation. COOKIE_JAR is a local file readable only by your user. KUBE_TOKEN is the bearer token of the Kubernetes caller.

tags.name: performance
tags.description: Use these native JSON endpoints on the installed Web API to profile a workload. Set WEB_ORIGIN to the installation HTTPS origin and WORKSPACE to its Kubernetes namespace. The examples use a Kubernetes bearer token in KUBE_TOKEN. A browser with a session can send its cookie, the configured Origin, and X-Prokrust-CSRF: 1. OIDC browser calls also send X-Prokrust-Context with the selected context ID. The caller needs Kubernetes access to each resource it reads or changes. The request body limit is 16 KiB. For Download, set CAPTURE_FILE to the desired local output path.

tags.name: web-health
tags.description: The installation uses these endpoints as Kubernetes probes on the Web API listener. They report the state of this service. Inspect the readiness status of the individual workspace resource for workload health.

Identity.description: Claims for the signed-in OIDC identity.

provider.description: ID of the configured provider used for this login.

subject.description: Stable subject identifier for this issuer.

email.description: Email claim, or null when the provider supplies none.

groups.description: Group names obtained at login and made available to access rules.

Context.description: An eligible workspace and service account. Select one for a browser request.

id.description: Opaque context ID. Send this value in X-Prokrust-Context for requests made with the OIDC session.

namespace.description: Name of the workspace Kubernetes namespace. Use the namespace that contains the target resource.

namespace_uid.description: UID of this workspace namespace. A recreated namespace has a different UID.

service_account.description: Name of the Kubernetes service account selected by the access rules.

service_account_uid.description: UID of that service account instance.

display_name.description: Display label configured for this grant. Use it when showing available workspaces.

OidcSession.description: OIDC session and its current grants.

contexts.description: Currently eligible workspace contexts. An empty array means this identity has no matching access binding.

expires_in_seconds.description: Seconds until this login expires. The limit is one hour or the ID token expiry, whichever comes first.

error.description: Application reason, such as invalid_callback or context_revoked.

code.description: Transport error category, such as unauthenticated or permission_denied.

CaptureError.description: Failure from the native capture handler.

message.description: Reason the request failed. Inspect workspace permissions, the current target UID, or the artifact state it identifies.

TargetRef.description: Workspace workload and its exact Kubernetes identity. [PerformanceCapture fields](/reference/kubernetes/platform.prokrust.ai/v1beta1/performancecapture/)

kind.description: Select the workload type. ConnectorService means the Service belonging to an installation-managed connector.

name.description: Kubernetes name of the workload or connector Service in this workspace.

uid.description: Kubernetes UID of that target. Read it from metadata.uid so a replacement cannot be profiled by mistake.

attemptUid.description: Limit the capture to one execution attempt when the workload has retried.

podUid.description: Use the UID returned by Targets to select a specific pod.

containerName.description: Use the name from Targets to select one container in that pod.

workspaceUid.description: Required string in the submitted shape. Pass an empty string as the Web app does. The server replaces it with the workspace namespace UID before creation.

mode.description: Choose Cpu for a running process or Cuda for a training capture armed before the selected steps.

durationSeconds.description: Length of a CPU capture window in seconds.

sampleRateHz.description: CPU sample frequency in Hz. Lower the rate to collect fewer samples.

trigger.description: Optional CUDA training window. Use step numbers for the current runtime.

stage.description: Reserved stage selector. The CUDA controller reports a stage or epoch trigger as unsupported; use step-based triggers.

stepCount.description: Number of training steps to record.

epoch.description: Reserved epoch selector. Select firstStep and stepCount instead; the CUDA controller reports a stage or epoch trigger as unsupported.

Capture.description: Kubernetes PerformanceCapture returned by the API server. Use metadata.name and metadata.uid for later requests, and status.phase, status.artifact, and status.flamegraph to locate results. [Full resource fields and status](/reference/kubernetes/platform.prokrust.ai/v1beta1/performancecapture/)

Flame.description: Verified JSON profile returned from the profiling backend. The backend can supply additional format fields.

flamegraph.description: Tree encoded as a frame-name table and depth levels.

names.description: Frame names referred to by the level entries.

values.description: Encoded frame offsets, widths, self counts, and indexes into names in the profiling backend format.

total.description: Total sampled weight. A zero count means no samples were collected.

KubernetesBearer.description: Kubernetes bearer token for the caller.
